First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\sin {2\theta}=2\sin \theta \cos \theta
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the double-angle formula for the hyperbolic sine:

$$
\sinh {2\theta} =2\sinh \theta \cosh \theta
$$

 

Letting $\theta= 2x,$ we get

$$
\sinh {4x} =2\sinh 2x \cosh 2x.
$$

 

Rearranging the above formula, we get

$$
\dfrac{1}{2}\sinh {4x}= \sinh 2x \cosh 2x.
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =\int 4\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 2\operatorname{sinh}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \operatorname{sinh}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cosh}⁡4x+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡4x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
